speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help diagnose your condition, can you describe the appearance of the rash on your trunk and extremities, and when did the fever and other symptoms begin?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: The timeline of a prodrome followed by a rash sparing the perioral area is highly suggestive of Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease). Does she have any known history of hemolytic anemia, such as sickle cell disease, which could complicate this condition?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical presentation of a prodrome followed by a facial rash sparing the perioral area and then spreading to the trunk is classic for Erythema Infectiosum. I am confident in this assessment based on the distinctive "slapped cheek" appearance and subsequent spread. DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease)
